_comment: Cost CLASS for every row of the licensed-API usage ledger (MEMORY/api_usage.jsonl), read by WebPivot/tools/api_usage.py `report`. The ledger counts roughly one unit per call for every provider, including free reverse-WHOIS previews and keyless lookups, so a single total reads like a bill when it is not one. Each row is put in exactly one class: `free` (nothing billed: previews, keyless/self-hosted calls, rejected requests), `quota` (a capped plan that resets on its own, like urlscan's daily/monthly allowance or a free-tier monthly credit pool; spending it costs throughput, not money), or `metered` (each call draws down purchased credits or is billed per request). The report prints one subtotal per class and labels the overall total 'estimated units'. Lookup order: `action_classes` (provider:action), then `provider_classes`, then `rules.default_class`. An unknown provider falls into `metered`, so it over-states cost and never hides it. Edit this file to reclassify a provider for your own plan; no code change is needed.

rules._comment: default_class: the class for a provider not listed below (keep it `metered` so an unclassified spend is never under-stated). zero_credit_is_free: a row that recorded 0 credits (a keyless call, such as ipinfo with no token, or a rejected 4xx/5xx request that record() zeroes) counts as `free` whatever its provider.

action_classes._comment: Per-action overrides as `provider:action`. These are checked before provider_classes. WhoisXML reverse-WHOIS mode=preview returns only a count and is not billed, so whois_enrich._wx_action() labels it `reverse-whois-preview`. WHOIS-history preview is left at its provider's class (metered) because WhoisXML charges 1 DRS credit for it (see tools/domain_table.py --whois-history).

provider_classes._comment: Provider class, using the provider name passed to api_usage.record(). `metered` providers draw down purchased credits per call (WhoisXML DRS, FOFA points, DNSlytics, IntelX per-search credits). `quota` providers sit on a capped plan that resets (urlscan, Censys monthly pool, Shodan monthly query credits, SerpApi monthly searches, and others). `free` providers are keyless, self-hosted or log at 0 credits by design (crt.sh, CIRCL pSSL, RDAP, CertKit, CertIndex, GitHub, Quarry, MISP).
